novel_features.name: Project burn + projection
novel_features.description: See which projects have burned >80% of budget with a projected exhaust date based on 4-week velocity.
novel_features.rationale: Joins projects.budget with aggregated time_entries — no single API call returns burn % with velocity-based projection; harvest-toolkit only does flat reports.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer 'which projects are about to blow their budget?' in one call — exit code 2 makes it cron-friendly.

novel_features.name: Notes full-text search
novel_features.description: FTS5 search across all your time-entry notes, with filters for user/project/date.
novel_features.rationale: SQLite FTS5 over locally-synced time_entries.notes — no Harvest API endpoint supports text search, and no competing tool offers offline FTS.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to recall what you logged without re-paginating the API or scrolling Harvest's web UI.

novel_features.name: Timesheet gap detection
novel_features.description: List workdays where a user logged less than a threshold (default 6 hours), to chase missing time.
novel_features.rationale: Joins users × time_entries × workday calendar locally; surfaces 'who has gaps this week' that no competitor exposes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this on Friday to chase missing entries without manual CSV exports.

novel_features.name: Client margin / realization
novel_features.description: Per-client revenue (billable hours × billable_rate) minus cost (hours × cost_rate), with realization %.
novel_features.rationale: Joins time_entries × billable_rates × cost_rates × clients locally — Harvest API exposes the rates but not the joined margin.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer 'is client X profitable?' without exporting to a spreadsheet.

novel_features.name: Utilization trend
novel_features.description: Billable percentage per user over a range, with rolling 4-week trend.
novel_features.rationale: Local group-by on time_entries.billable per ISO week per user; the agency-defining KPI that no CLI surfaces.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to monitor team utilization trends without rebuilding Google Sheets pivots.

novel_features.name: Day reconstruction stubs
novel_features.description: For a given user+date, emit JSON stub entries that fill the day to target hours, proportional to that user's recent project mix.
novel_features.rationale: Reads existing entries, computes deficit, generates stubs from recent project ratio — mechanical, pipes into `time-entries create --stdin`.
novel_features.example: harvest-pp-cli day reconstruct --user me --date 2026-05-14 --target-hours 8 --json | harvest-pp-cli time-entries create --stdin --dry-run
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for Friday backfill — generate plausible stubs, edit notes, then commit.

novel_features.name: Entry repeat
novel_features.description: Repost an existing time entry to a new date or N consecutive workdays with the same project/task/hours/notes.
novel_features.rationale: Idempotent via natural key (user+date+project+task+notes-hash); skips dates that already have a matching entry.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for recurring work (standup, planning) — one command per week instead of typing the same flags daily.

novel_features.name: Local reconcile
novel_features.description: Diff local SQLite vs the Harvest API for a date range; surface rows that drifted (edits made after the last sync).
novel_features.rationale: Re-fetches the range, compares against local snapshot, prints drifted IDs and field-level changes — supports cron-driven workflows that the MCP servers can't.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this nightly to detect retroactive edits and trigger re-aggregation for stale dashboards.

narrative.headline: Every Harvest CLI feature, plus a local SQLite store and offline FTS no other tool has.
narrative.value_prop: Every feature in hrvst-cli, hcl, and the MCP servers — for time entries, projects, invoices, and reports — plus offline full-text search over your notes, project burn projection, client margin, utilization trends, and timesheet-gap detection. All built on a synced local SQLite store so cron-driven scripts and AI agents can query without hammering the rate-limited API.
narrative.auth_narrative: Harvest uses Personal Access Tokens (PATs). Set `HARVEST_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `HARVEST_ACCOUNT_ID` in your environment, or run `harvest-pp-cli auth set-token` to store them locally. `harvest-pp-cli doctor` validates the token and surfaces the authenticated user.

quickstart.comment: Validates HARVEST_ACCESS_TOKEN + HARVEST_ACCOUNT_ID and confirms the API is reachable.
Populates the local SQLite store with all time entries, projects, clients, users, tasks.
Sanity check that the right account is wired up.
Demo of the offline FTS feature.
List active projects burning >80% of budget — exit 2 if any.
Friday chase: who has gaps this week.

troubleshoots.fix: Check HARVEST_ACCESS_TOKEN is set (`harvest-pp-cli auth status`). Tokens are personal-access-tokens, NOT OAuth bearer tokens — get one at https://id.getharvest.com/developers.

troubleshoots.symptom: 404 Not Found on a known-good account
troubleshoots.fix: Confirm HARVEST_ACCOUNT_ID matches the account that owns the PAT. Account IDs are numeric; tokens are per-account.
Harvest limits to 100 requests / 15-second window. The CLI retries with backoff; for large backfills add `--rate-limit-window 15s` or run during off-hours.
Use `sync --since YYYY-MM-DD` or `sync --resources time-entries` for targeted refreshes. The full sync hits every endpoint with `updated_since` cursors.
FTS index is populated by `sync`. Run `sync --resources time-entries` first; the SQLite FTS5 index lives in your local DB.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for harvest-pp-cli when you need to query Harvest data programmatically — cron scripts that fan out across many entries, AI agents asking 'what did I do last week,' invoicing automations that join time entries with rates, or any task where the rate-limited API would be too slow. For interactive time-entry CRUD an agent could call the API directly; use this CLI when the local store, FTS, or cross-entity joins matter.

recipes.title: Friday timesheet chase
recipes.explanation: Run on Friday to surface every team member with gaps for the current week, in agent-friendly JSON. (Sync first with: harvest-pp-cli sync --resources time-entries)

recipes.title: Project burn alert (cron)
recipes.command: harvest-pp-cli project burn --threshold 80 --json --select project,client,pct_used,projected_exhaust_date || echo 'project budget breach'
recipes.explanation: Cron-friendly — exit 2 when any active project crosses 80% used. Pipe to Slack or PagerDuty.

recipes.title: Find that auth-refactor entry
recipes.explanation: FTS5 over your local notes — finds entries without paginating the API.

recipes.title: Recurring weekly work
recipes.explanation: Dry-run shows what would be posted. Drop --dry-run to commit. Idempotent — re-running skips dates already filled.

recipes.title: Month-end realization check (deep --select)
recipes.explanation: Joins time entries × rates × client locally. Use the dotted `--select` paths to pull only the fields your dashboard needs.
